subject: Post-call: TCO & token economics recap for ACME - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: TCO & token economics (ACME)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Jordan — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned.

Attendees:
- Jordan Lee (ACME)
- Marissa Cole (Redwood)
- Rishi Malhotra (Redwood, SE)

Key pain points & goals you shared:
- Current LLM spend unpredictability: spikes during product launches causing monthly overruns (~$40k/month average, peak $68k).
- Need to reduce per-inference unit cost while keeping response quality intact for customer-facing workflows.
- Target: scale to ~1M inference calls/month with a budget constraint of ~$25k/month for inference cost.
- Latency SLO: <250ms p95 for short chat flows.

What we discussed (high level):
- Token economics: you’re currently on a per-request model with long prompts (avg 680 tokens/request). Biggest wins are prompt engineering + prefix caching to reduce average billed tokens.
- Batching & KV caching: for ACME’s bursty traffic pattern, combining 2–4x effective batching during steady state plus prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts should reduce token compute by ~30–45%.
- Model/quantization tradeoffs: moving to a 4-bit quantized variant for background jobs and a 8-bit warmed model for low-latency paths preserves quality while cutting GPU cycles.
- Deployment options: short pilot on Hosted API to validate savings, followed by Dedicated reservation if we hit predictable throughput and want guaranteed latency.

Preliminary TCO framing (back-of-envelope):
- Current observed (ACME-provided): ~$40k/mo baseline (varies).
- With batching + prefix caching + quantized model mix (conservative): estimated 30% reduction -> ~$28k/mo.
- With aggressive optimization (prompt reductions, cache hit improvements to 40–50%): estimated 40–55% reduction -> ~$18k–24k/mo.
- Additional fixed costs if you move to Dedicated reserved nodes (monthly commit): depends on committed level; we’ll model a 6–9 month ROI window in the deck.

Attachments I’ve included: redwood-tco-summary.pdf (high-level assumptions & savings model), acme-mru-estimates.xlsx (token/usage assumptions you provided + our baseline calc).

Immediate next steps
- I’ll send the detailed TCO deck and per-scenario line items (attached). (Action: Marissa)
- Can you confirm the primary procurement contact we should loop in? You mentioned there’s a $25k/month ceiling to work within.
- If possible, share a 2-week sample of anonymized request logs (no PII) so Rishi can run a quick batching/cache simulation (aiming to have results in 5 business days after receipt).
- Suggest scheduling a 30-min pilot plan review with your engineering + procurement for week of 9/27.

Thanks — happy to trim or expand any of the sections above.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
